title: auth/header: unify project/org keys, scoped tokens, nonce signing, and CORS for OpenAI-compat
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Clarifies auth header semantics and introduces X-Redwood-Nonce request signing header; backwards compatible with legacy API keys. Operators should ensure CORS policies allow Authorization and X-Redwood-Nonce when using scoped tokens.
description: This PR standardizes Authorization header semantics across the Redwood API surface and the OpenAI compatibility middleware. Motivation: multiple customer support tickets and an internal audit showed inconsistent behavior when mixing project-level keys, org-level keys, and scoped short-lived tokens, particularly when streaming and when clients use strict CORS policies. This change unifies parsing rules, documents precedence (project key > org key > scoped token unless explicit scope), and adds an optional X-Redwood-Nonce header for signed requests to protect against replay in high-security flows. The PR also updates CORS handling to explicitly expose Authorization and X-Redwood-Nonce for browser clients and improves OpenAI-compat middleware so that streaming endpoints correctly forward the effective principal and scoped claims for tool/function-calling flows. Checklist: 1) implement unified parser and precedence rules; 2) add X-Redwood-Nonce validation and retry-safe verification; 3) update OpenAI-compat header mapping and compatibility tests; 4) add docs and migration notes; 5) run and stabilize streaming integration tests. Backwards compatibility: default behavior for existing API keys is preserved; scoped tokens require explicit scope claims and are validated as before. Impact: customers using custom CORS whitelists must allow the new nonce header; SSO/clients that expect legacy header ordering should be unaffected but are advised to adopt the explicit precedence. Testing: unit tests, integration streaming tests, and an internal canary against staging dedicated pools. See linked Linear items for rollout plan and ops runbook.

review_comments: Marco Chen: Please clarify precedence table for project vs org keys; I expect explicit project keys to override org but we need test coverage for mixed headers. Aisha: Confirmed in parser and added tests in streaming_auth_test.go.
Ruth Walters: Can you document the nonce replay window and how it interacts with clock skew? Aisha: Added details and configurable env var REDWOOD_NONCE_WINDOW_SECONDS with default 300; note in docs.

Diego Morales: Integration tests flaked on the first run for streaming aborts when nonce validation returned 409; we should make validation idempotent for retried client requests. Aisha: Adjusted verifier to accept retry-safe idempotency token for deterministic retried streams.

Security review (Lara Singh): Approve pending addition of telemetry tags for rejected nonces for incident troubleshooting. Aisha: Added telemetry tag 'auth_nonce_reject' and logged sample context. Marco Chen: LGTM and approved the PR.

change_log_entry: Auth: Standardize Authorization header semantics across project/org/scoped tokens; add X-Redwood-Nonce for optional request signing; update CORS exposure. Backwards compatible with existing keys.
notes_for_ops: Rollout plan: 1) deploy to staging and run integration streaming suite, 2) enable canary for 5% of hosted traffic, 3) monitor auth_nonce_reject and streaming error rates for 48h, 4) if regressions occur rollback toggle for nonce validation. Config knobs: REDWOOD_NONCE_WINDOW_SECONDS, REDWOOD_ALLOW_LEGACY_HEADER_ORDER=false.
migration_guide: For most customers no action required. If you use browser-based integrations and strict CORS allowlists, add Authorization and X-Redwood-Nonce to Access-Control-Expose-Headers. If you generate scoped tokens, ensure the token carries the correct scope claim for streaming/tool-calling endpoints. See docs/auth-header-semantics.md for examples.
